name: curl
summary: Transfer data from or to a URL, within the web access the application allows
help: Usage: curl [options...] <url>...
Fetch each URL and write the response body to standard output.
-d, --data <data>          send <data> in a POST body (@FILE reads a file, @- stdin; newlines dropped)
--data-binary <data>   like --data, but the file is sent exactly as it is
--data-raw <data>      like --data, but @ has no special meaning
--data-urlencode <d>   like --data, URL-encoding the value (name=value, =value, value)
--json <data>          send <data> as JSON (sets Content-Type and Accept)
-G, --get                  send the --data values as a query string in a GET
-X, --request <method>     use <method> instead of GET or POST
-H, --header <header>      add a request header ("Name: value")
-A, --user-agent <name>    set the User-Agent header
-u, --user <user:pass>     use HTTP basic authentication
-L, --location             follow redirects
--max-redirs <num>     follow at most <num> redirects
-i, --include              print the response headers before the body
-I, --head                 send a HEAD request and print the headers
-o, --output <file>        write the body to <file> instead of standard output
-O, --remote-name          write the body to a file named like the URL's last part
-f, --fail                 exit 22 without printing the body when the status is 400 or more
--fail-with-body       like --fail, but print the body
-s, --silent               print no error messages
-S, --show-error           print error messages even with --silent
-w, --write-out <format>   print <format> after the transfer, e.g. '%{http_code}'
-m, --max-time <seconds>   give up after <seconds>
--retry <num>          try again up to <num> times after a timeout or an answer saying try later
--retry-delay <sec>    wait <sec> between tries (default: 1, then twice as long each time)
--retry-max-time <sec> start no new try after <sec>
--retry-all-errors     try again after any error
--retry-connrefused    also try again when the connection is refused
--proto <protocols>    only use these protocols (e.g. =https)
--proto-redir <protos> only follow redirects to these protocols
--fail-early           stop at the first URL that fails
--compressed           ask for a compressed response and decompress it
-v, --verbose              print the request and response headers on standard error
-k, --insecure             accepted and ignored: certificates are always verified
--tlsv1.2, --tlsv1.3, --tls-max, --http1.1, --http2, --ssl-reqd, --no-progress-meter, -#
accepted and ignored
-h, --help                 show this help
-V, --version              show the version
The application decides which sites can be reached; others fail like an unknown host.

exitCodes.1: unsupported or disallowed protocol, or a request the web policy refuses
exitCodes.6: host not resolved, or not allowed by the web policy
exitCodes.7: could not connect (an IP address the web policy refuses)
exitCodes.8: the server's reply could not be read: a malformed status line or header
exitCodes.18: the body ended before its Content-Length or last chunk; what came is written
exitCodes.22: --fail and a status of 400 or more
exitCodes.23: could not write the output file
exitCodes.26: could not read a data file
exitCodes.52: the server closed the connection without a response
exitCodes.63: response larger than the web policy allows

notes: The reason* messages are the web policy's reasons, shared with wget (WebSession builds them). Registered in every shell; without a web policy (Shell.AllowWeb and the ports' equivalents) every host fails to resolve, as on a machine without a network. No progress meter is printed. Warnings (curl's "Warning: " lines) are wrapped at 79 columns as curl does when standard error is not a terminal. Without --fail-early the exit status is the last URL's. Malformed responses: a body shorter than its Content-Length, or a chunked body cut short, is written as far as it came and fails with 18 (a redirect is then not followed); a longer body is cut at its Content-Length; any number of 100 Continue responses is skipped; a chunk size that is not hex fails with 56, and nothing of that body is written (curl writes what came before it); an unreadable status line or a header line without a colon fails with 8 (curl says 1 for some status lines); no response at all fails with 52.
